'''''Muehlenbeckia axillaris''''' (creeping wire vine, sprawling wire vine, matted lignum) is a low evergreen shrub, forming wiry mats up to about {{convert|1|m}} in diameter, native to [[New Zealand]], and the Australian states of [[Tasmania]], [[New South Wales]] and [[Victoria (Australia)|Victoria]].<ref name=NSW>{{cite web|url= http://plantnet.rbgsyd.nsw.gov.au/cgi-bin/NSWfl.pl?page=nswfl&lvl=sp&name=Muehlenbeckia~axillaris|title=''Muehlenbeckia axillaris'' |accessdate=2009-03-08|work=PlantNET - New South Wales Flora Online|publisher= Royal Botanic Gardens & Domain Trust, Sydney Australia}}</ref> It has thin, red-brown stems, with glossy squarish to roundish leaves that are less than {{convert|1|cm|abbr=on}} in diameter and {{convert|2|–|4|mm|abbr=on}} thick. Flowers are inconspicuous, yellowish-white, {{convert|4|-|8|mm|abbr=on}} in diameter, and borne in groups of up to three in the axils. The fruit is black, shiny, and up to {{convert|3.5|mm|abbr=on}} long, produced in late summer to fall.

The plant is hardy, drought-tolerant, and quick-growing, thriving in a range of light conditions. It can be cultivated as a ground cover and grows well in rocky ground, as well as standard potting soil. Although it grows fastest in warm seasons, it tolerates freezing weather.
[[File:Muehlenbeckia axillaris fruiting.jpg|alt=Muehlenbeckia axillaris fruiting. Multiple stages of ripeness can be seen.|thumb|Fruiting in [[Arthur's Pass National Park]]. Multiple stages of fruit development and even a couple of flowers can be seen in this image.]]

==Taxonomy==
The species was first described by [[Joseph Dalton Hooker]] in 1847, who used the name "''Polygonum'' (''Muhlenbeckia'') ''axillaris''".<ref name=Hook47>{{Citation |mode=cs1|last1=Hooker |first1=W.J. |date=1847 |contribution=Polygoneae |title=London Journal of Botany |volume=6 |page=278 |contribution-url=https://biodiversitylibrary.org/page/2926252 |accessdate=2019-03-06 }}</ref> Both [[Stephan Endlicher]] (in 1848)<ref name="IPNI_151752-3">{{cite web |title=Plant Name Details for ''Muehlenbeckia axillaris'' (Hook.f.) Endl. |work=[[International Plant Names Index|The International Plant Names Index]] |url=http://www.ipni.org/ipni/idPlantNameSearch.do?id=151752-3 |accessdate=2019-03-06 }}</ref> and [[Wilhelm Gerhard Walpers]] (in 1849)<ref name="IPNI_694740-1">{{cite web |title=Plant Name Details for ''Muehlenbeckia axillaris'' |work=[[International Plant Names Index|The International Plant Names Index]] |url=http://www.ipni.org/ipni/idPlantNameSearch.do?id=694740-1 |accessdate=2019-03-06 }}</ref> later referred to it as just ''Muehlenbeckia axillaris''.
